The packages can install and update without errors, so the warning message is cosmetic.\\n\\nIf you packages fail to install, then there are repository issues. Or, you might receive errors such as \\\"Cannot find a valid baseurl for repo\\\" or \\\"Error: Failed to download metadata for repo\\\". These issues occur when there are RHUI connectivity, network configuration, or RHUI certificate issues. They aren't related to the **subscription-manager** registration. To resolve these issues, check your RHUI client configuration, network access to RHUI endpoints, and certificate validity. To troubleshoot repository errors, see [Why do I receive errors when I use yum on my Amazon EC2 instance that runs RHEL?](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ec2-yum-rhel-errors)\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/amazon-ec2-not-registered-warning-red-hat\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Red Hat FAQs\",\"context\":\"### If I launch Red Hat Enterprise Linux on Amazon EC2 instances in an Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), how do I access the Red Hat Update Infrastructure (RHUI)?\\n\\nAll on-demand Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) are configured to utilize the Red Hat Update Infrastructure (RHUI) in AWS. If in a VPC, Amazon EC2 RHEL instances will need to access RHUI in EC2 either through the VPC Internet Gateway, through an attached Virtual IP, or through a VPN or Direct Connect connection to a data center that routes the update request through the general internet to the RHUI servers.\\n\\nIf you would rather get updates from an on-premises update repository, like Red Hat Network Satellite, then you will need to have an account with Red Hat and purchase entitlements to their Cloud Access AMIs through this license mobility program. These entitlements come in the form of the traditional annual subscriptions.\\n\\nOnce deployed using the Cloud Access AMIs, de-register your instance and re-register to your on-premises update infrastructure. Note, however, that in this set up you will incur additional network charges for data transfer out of AWS. Avoiding these network charges is one of the benefits of using the in cloud Red Hat Update Infrastructure.\\n\\nSteps to de-register and re-register:\\n\\n1. Edit the /etc/yum.repos.d/redhat-rhui-client-config.repo and change 'enabled=1' to 'enabled=0\u2019\\n2. Edit the /etc/yum.repos.d/redhat-rhui.repo and change 'enabled=1' to 'enabled=0\u2019 for all repository entries\\n3. Edit /etc/yum/pluginconf.d/rhnplugin.conf and change 'enabled=0' to 'enabled=1'\\n4. {"id": "1ea44ac9-0aa3-4e00-a5bb-51df7d259a5d", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_LAi4OSxb3ajlE3irPMcgpP", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"status\":\"SUCCESS\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ec2-yum-rhel-errors\",\"content\":\"# Why do I receive errors when I use yum on my Amazon EC2 instance that runs RHEL?\\n\\nI want to use yum on my Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance that runs Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), but I receive errors.\\n\\n---\\n\\nShort description\\n-----------------\\n\\nAfter you run a yum command on your EC2 instance, you might receive an error. To determine what error occurred, use the output messages of the yum command. Then, use the resolution method that best fits your error message.\\n\\nResolution\\n----------\\n\\n### Connection timed out or failed to download packages error\\n\\nError: \\\"Connection timed out XXXX milliseconds or failed to download the packages.\\\"\\n\\nTo resolve this error, complete the following steps:\\n\\n1. Verify that the [security group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-security-groups.html) that's attached to your EC2 instance allows outbound HTTP and HTTPS traffic.\\n2. Verify that the network access control lists (network ACLs) that are associated with your instance's subnet allow outbound HTTP and HTTPS traffic. See the following example of network ACL rules:\\n    ```plaintext\\n    Inbound rules  Rule#    Type                    Protocol    Port Range    Source        Allow/Deny\\n    130      Custom TCP Rule         TCP (6)     1024-65535    0.0.0.0/0     ALLOW\\n    140      Custom TCP Rule         TCP (6)     1024-65535    ::/0          ALLOW\\n    *        ALL Traffic             ALL         ALL           0.0.0.0/0     DENY\\n    *        ALL Traffic             ALL         ALL           ::/0          DENY\\n      \\n      \\n    Outbound rules  \\n    Rule #    Type                   Protocol    Port Range    Destination  Allow/Deny\\n    100       HTTP (80)              TCP (6)     80            0.0.0.0/0    ALLOW\\n    101       HTTPS (443)            TCP (6)     443           0.0.0.0/0    ALLOW\\n    102       HTTP (80)              TCP (6)     80            ::/0         ALLOW\\n    103       HTTPS (443)            TCP (6)     443           ::/0         ALLOW\\n    *         ALL Traffic            ALL         ALL           ::/0         DENY\\n    *         ALL Traffic            ALL         ALL           0.0.0.0/0    DENY\\n    ```\\n    \\n    In the preceding example, Rule 100 and Rule 101 in the outbound rules correspond to Rule 130 in the inbound rules. Rule 102 and Rule 103 in the outbound rules correspond to Rule 140 in the inbound rules. The allowed outbound traffic on port 80 and port 443 (HTTP and HTTPS) is matched with the allowed inbound traffic on the ephemeral ports.\\n    \\n    The example network ACL uses an ephemeral port range of 1024-65535. The type of client that you use or communicate with determines the range for your network ACLs. To cover the different types of clients that might initiate traffic to public-facing instances in your virtual private cloud (VPC), open ephemeral ports 1024-65535. You can also add rules to the network ACL that deny traffic on any malicious ports within that range. Make sure that you place the **deny** rules earlier in the table than the **allow** rules that open the wide range of ephemeral ports.\\n    \\n    For more information, see [Ephemeral ports](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-network-acls.html#nacl-ephemeral-ports) and [Custom network ACL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-network-acls.html#custom-network-acl).\\n    \\n3. Verify that your instance has access to RHEL repositories.\\n    \\n    If your instance is in a public subnet with an internet gateway, then see\u00a0[Configuration for internet access](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_Internet_Gateway.html#vpc-igw-internet-access).\\n    \\n    If your instance is in a private subnet with a NAT gateway, then see\u00a0[NAT gateways](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat-gateway.html).\\n    \\n    If your instance is in a private subnet with a NAT instance, then see [NAT instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_NAT_Instance.html).\\n    \\n    If your instance is in a public or private subnet with an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) VPC endpoint, then see\u00a0[How can we update a disconnected or an air-gapped system (A system without internet connection)?](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/29269) on the Red Hat website.\\n    \\n    If your instance is in a private subnet with a proxy, then configure yum to use a proxy. Modify the **/etc/yum.conf** file with the following parameters. In this example, replace **proxy-port**, **proxy-user-name**, and **proxy-password** with the correct values for your proxy:\\n    \\n    ```plaintext\\n    proxy=http://proxy-server-IP-address:proxy_port\\n    proxy_username=\\\"proxy-user-name\\\"  \\n    proxy_password=\\\"proxy-password\\\"\\n    ```\\n    \\n4. To confirm that the instance can access the repository, run the following command:\\n    ```plaintext\\n    sudo yum check-update\\n    ```\\n    If the command successfully retrieves package information without errors, then your instance can access the repositories.\\n    \\n    If you encounter errors, check the repository configuration files in the\u00a0**/etc/yum.repos.d/** directory to make sure that they're configured correctly. Then, confirm that your instance is in a public subnet with the appropriate security group rules to allow outbound internet traffic.\\n    \\n\\n### **Could not contact any CDS load balancers error**\\n\\nError: \\\"Could not contact any CDS load balancers.\\\"\\n\\nTo resolve this error, launch an EC2 instance with the newest version of the same RHEL release as your instance.\\n\\n1. To download the newest RHUI client package, log in to the new instance, and then run the following command:  \\n    ```plaintext\\n    $ sudo yum install --downloadonly --downloaddir=/root/ rh-amazon-rhui-client.noarch\\n    ```\\n    \\n2. Copy the downloaded rpm package to the instance. Then, run the following commands:  \\n    ```plaintext\\n    $ sudo yum remove -y rh-amazon-rhui-client  \\n    $ sudo rpm -ivh --nodeps /path/to/rpmfile/rh-amazon-rhui-client*\\n    ```\\n    **Note:** Replace **/path/to/rpmfile** with the file path that you copied the file to.\\n3. After you install the package, you must reinstall it to get all the dependencies:\\n    ```plaintext\\n    $ sudo yum reinstall -y rh-amazon-rhui-client\\n    ```\\n    \\n4. Download the required packages from RHUI:  \\n    ```plaintext\\n    $ sudo yum clean all\\n    $ sudo yum repolist\\n    $ sudo yum list\\n    ```\\n    \\n\\n### \\\"Failure: Repodata/repomd.xml\\\" error or a similar \\\"404 - Not Found\\\" error\\n\\nError: \\\"Failure: repodata/repomd.xml from rhel-7-server-rhui-rh-common-rpms: \\\\[Errno 256\\\\] No more mirrors to try or https://rhui3.eu-west-1.aws.ce.redhat.com/pulp/repos/content/dist/rhel/rhui/server/7/7/x86\\\\_64/rh-common/os/repodata/repomd.xml : \\\\[Errno 14\\\\] HTTPS Error 404 - Not Found\\\"\\n\\nThis error occurs for the following reasons:\\n\\n*   Corrupted yum cache\\n*   Inaccessible repository URL caused by network-related issues\\n*   Customized or other media repositories\\n*   Outdated allowlist when you use an IP-based firewall configuration to access Red Hat's Content Delivery Network (CDN)\\n\\nTo remove and then rebuild the yum cache, run the following commands:\\n\\n```plaintext\\n# rm -rf /var/cache/yum/*\\n# yum clean all\\n# yum check-update\\n# yum repolist enabled\\n```\\n\\nFor more information, see [Troubleshooting '\\\\[Errno 14\\\\] HTTPS Error 404 - Not Found' error observed on Red Hat Satellite 6 clients](https://access.redhat.com/articles/5140651) on the Red Hat website.\\n\\n### This system is not registered with an entitlement server error\\n\\nError: \\\"This system is not registered with an entitlement server. You can use subscription-manager to register.\\\"\\n\\nTo resolve this error, use **subscription-manager** to register the system. When you run an instance from the AWS Marketplace, that instance includes an embedded billing product in the metadata that Red Hat provides. When Red Hat connects to the RHUI repositories that AWS uses, Red Hat uses the billing product to check for a valid subscription.\\n\\nTo check the billing product on an instance, run the following command:\\n\\n```plaintext\\n$ TOKEN=`curl -X PUT \\\"http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token\\\" -H \\\"X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 21600\\\"` \\\\\\n&& curl -H \\\"X-aws-ec2-metadata-token: $TOKEN\\\" http://169.254.169.254/latest/dynamic/instance-identity/document -q 2>/dev/null | grep billingProducts\\n\\n  \\\"billingProducts\\\" : [ \\\"bp-6fa54006\\\" ],\\n```\\n\\nIf your instance has the required billing code, then ignore the message from **subscription-manager**. If you don't want to see the message, set the\u00a0**subscription-manager** plugin from **/etc/yum/pluginconf.d/subscription-manager.conf** to **enabled=0**. Run the following command:\\n\\n```plaintext\\nsudo vi  /etc/yum/pluginconf.d/subscription-manager.conf\\nenabled=0\\n```\\n\\nThen, save and quit the configuration file.\\n\\n**Note:** If you migrate your instance or create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from snapshots, then the billing product isn't available. If you use a **CreateImage** from an existing instance that has a billing code, then the new AMI inherits this information. The AMI can now communicate with the RHUI repositories.\",\"total_length\":9085,\"start_index\":0,\"end_index\":9085,\"truncated\":false,\"redirected_url\":null,\"error_code\":null}]}}"}]}], "label": "Running Verify Aws Claim"}

Importing the key manually usually isn't the real fix here — on RHUI repos the key AWS/Red Hat ships is tied to specific repo config files, and a stale cache or mismatched repo file is the more common culprit. Here's what to check next, in order:

**1. Confirm which key the repo is actually configured to use**
```
dnf repoinfo rhel-8-baseos-rhui-rpms | grep -i gpgkey
cat /etc/yum.repos.d/redhat-rhui.repo | grep -A3 baseos
```
Make sure `gpgkey=` in the `.repo` file points at a key file that actually exists at that path (`rpm -q gpg-pubkey --qf '%{name}-%{version}-%{release} --> %{summary}\n'` to list imported keys and compare).

**2. Check for a stale/corrupted dnf cache** — this is the single most common cause of GPG failures that persist after a key import:
```
sudo dnf clean all
sudo rm -rf /var/cache/dnf
sudo dnf repolist enabled
```

**3. Check timestamp on the system clock.** GPG verification fails if the instance clock has drifted (common on instances that were stopped/started or restored from snapshot) — a key can appear "not yet valid" or "expired."
```
timedatectl
```

**4. Verify the `rh-amazon-rhui-client` package itself isn't stale or mismatched for the RHEL minor version** — RHUI client packages are versioned per RHEL point release, and an outdated client ships outdated/mismatched key references:
```
rpm -qa | grep rhui
sudo dnf reinstall -y rh-amazon-rhui-client
```

**5. Check if this instance was imaged or migrated (not launched fresh from the RHEL AMI).** If this instance was created via `CreateImage` from a snapshot, or BYOL→PAYG migration, the RHUI client bundled in the original AMI can be out of sync with what's now expected, and the billing product metadata that ties it to RHUI entitlement may be missing. Check:
```
TOKEN=$(curl -X PUT "http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token" -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 21600")
curl -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token: $TOKEN" http://169.254.169.254/latest/dynamic/instance-identity/document | grep billingProducts
```
If this comes back empty, the instance lost its PAYG billing code, which can cascade into RHUI client/cert mismatches.

**6. As a last resort, force dnf to re-verify against the correct key explicitly:**
```
sudo rpm --import /etc/pki/rpm-gpg/RPM-GPG-KEY-redhat-release
sudo dnf -y update --nogpgcheck   # only to confirm GPG is the sole blocker, not for production use
```
